key_insight: Claw-Eval-Live provides a live, refreshable benchmarking framework that evaluates LLM agents on evolving real-world workflows by separating a refreshable signal layer from static task definitions, enabling continuous, verifiable assessment of agent execution rather than just final responses.
problem_solved: Static benchmarks and single-shot final-response grading fail to capture changing workflow demand or verify whether agents actually executed tasks; this paper solves the need for continuous, execution-aware evaluation aligned with real-world workflow evolution.
method: Introduce a live benchmark that decouples a refreshable signal layer (sources of workflow demand and verification signals) from task definitions so signals can be updated across releases without changing core tasks.
Use automated execution verification (logs, action traces, and external service checks) to assess whether agents completed steps and adhered to real-world constraints, not just the final answer.
Continuously ingest public workflow-demand signals and versioned updates to evaluate agent robustness to evolving requirements and measure execution-level metrics (success rate, fidelity, recovery).
impact: Enables practitioners to benchmark agents against realistic, changing workflows and to trust evaluation results by verifying actual task execution—accelerating development of reliable production agents and more meaningful progress tracking.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agent interacts with tools/services; refreshable signal layer feeds verification signals and task updates into the benchmark.
Timeline showing periodic signal layer refreshes and how tasks evolve across releases (static tasks vs. dynamic signals).
Dashboard mockup: per-agent metrics (execution success, stepwise fidelity, recovery from failures) and comparison chart across releases.
Icon set: tools/services, logs/traces, shield/checkmark for verification, and refresh/clock for live updates.
paper_title: Claw-Eval-Live: A Live Agent Benchmark for Evolving Real-World Workflows
paper_authors: Chenxin Li, Zhengyang Tang, Huangxin Lin, Yunlong Lin, Shijue Huang
